options.description: The run continues with the next scripted request and the unanswered question is counted in the score. No model plays the owner. Recommended: You asked to see how much Haiku or Sonnet can do on its own, so an unanswered question scored as a gap is closest to that.
options.label: No answer, the question is logged as unanswered (Recommended)

options.description: A second model answers from a brief you write. Its answers can steer the run, and it may need a cap on exchanges.
options.label: A cheap model plays the owner from a hidden brief

payload.question:
When plumb asks a question during a benchmark run and no owner is there, who should answer it, and should there be a cap on how many questions or turns a run gets?

You said on 2026-10-21: "The idea is to be able from one plumb dev command like plumb evaluate simple or plumb evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using plumb tools."
payload.text: How can no owner be there exactly? There should always be a question owner in my opinion. A model answers the questions of the other one.
